1440.01 ESTABLISHMENT; DUTIES.
   Pursuant to Article IX of the City Charter and Chapters 4101:1-1 of the Ohio
Administrative Code, there is hereby established in and for the City a Division
of Buildings. The Division shall be responsible for all inspections of
construction work being performed in the Municipality, whether such
construction consists of new construction or additions and/or alterations to
existing structures. The Division shall also be responsible for checking into
and determining all violations of the Zoning Code (Ordinance 1970-232, passed
September 15, 1971) and all future amendments thereto, as well as all other
applicable City codes and ordinances. The Division shall have control of and be
responsible for the processing of all matters and details concerning the
construction of all residential, apartment, commercial and industrial
buildings, with the assistance of the City Engineer when his or her services
are requested. In addition to the foregoing areas of responsibility, the
Division shall have, as part of its function and authority, the control of the
inspection of all installations of sewer lines, water lines and gas lines and/
or connections of the same to existing facilities.
(Ord. 92-27. Passed 1-21-92; Ord. 05-180. Passed 12-5-05; Ord. 11-154. Passed
12-20-11.)
1440.02 COMPOSITION.
   The Division of Buildings shall consist of the following positions in
accordance with the Codified Ordinances of the City and the Ohio Administrative
Code Chapter 4101:1-1, Section 103.2:
   (a)   Building Official (Building Commissioner)
   (b)   Secretary
   (c)   Housing and Zoning Inspector
   (d)   Master Plans Examiner
   (e)   Certified Building Inspector, Electrical Inspector, Plumbing Inspector
and Backup Inspectors.
   Each of these positions in (a), (d) and (e) shall be filled in accordance
with the provisions of the Ohio Administrative Code 4101:1-1, Section 103.3
through Section 103.3.9.6.4 concerning qualification and education requirements
incidental to the efficient operation of the Division. Such personnel shall be
compensated in accordance with existing complement and compensation ordinances.
(Ord. 1973-50. Passed 3-7-73; Ord. 92-27. Passed 1-21-92; Ord. 05-180. Passed
12-5-05; Ord. 11-154. Passed 12-20-11.)
1440.03 BUILDING COMMISSIONER.
   (a)   Duties and Functions. The Building Commissioner shall:
      (1)   Review and evaluate all processes of inspection and be responsible
for the training of all building inspectors and the qualifications of all State
certified inspectors;
      (2)   Recommend policies and develop work programs;
      (3)   Work under the general supervision and direction of the Director of
Community Development;
      (4)   Enforce all applicable building requirements, codes, ordinances and
regulations of the Municipality;
      (5)   Be available for consultations with contractors, architects,
engineers and others who are engaged in either the design and/or construction
of structures to be constructed within the Municipality;
      (6)   Hear and investigate all complaints and violations pertaining to
the Building Code, the Zoning Code and all ordinances and regulations
pertaining to construction;
      (7)   Maintain, or cause to be maintained, accurate and adequate records
of all activities within the jurisdiction of the Division;
      (8)   Review all plans for construction and refer the same to the City
Engineer for his or her approval when the necessity arises;
      (9)   Confer with the Director of Community Development periodically to
ensure the enforcement of all Municipal ordinances, codes and regulations so as
to protect the health, safety and welfare of the inhabitants of the City;
      (10)   Be qualified to perform any and all duties of the various
inspectors when conditions warrant that such duties be done;
      (11)   Prepare all cases for prosecution when violations of City
ordinances occur, that the proper inspector of record be present in the proper
court of law when requested to testify as to such violations; and
      (12)   Attend all regular and/or special meetings of the Planning
Commission, the Board of Zoning Appeals and all other boards and commissions
when requested to do so or when his or her attendance is deemed necessary by
the Director of Community Development, Mayor or Council.
   (b)   Appointment; Term. The Building Commissioner shall be appointed by the
Mayor with the concurrence of a majority of the members elected to Council. The
position of Building Commissioner shall remain an appointive position and shall
not be included in the classified service.
(Ord. 1973-50. Passed 3-7-73; Ord. 92-27. Passed 1-21-92; Ord. 01-158. Passed
10-16-01; Ord. 02-24. Passed 4-16-02.)
   (c)   Benefits. The Building Commissioner shall receive the same benefits
received by other Municipal employees, except for overtime compensation.
(Ord. 1988-277. Passed 12-5-88; Ord. 05-180. Passed 12-5-05; Ord. 11-154.
Passed 12-20-11.)
1440.04 HOUSING AND ZONING INSPECTOR.
   The Housing and Zoning Inspector shall:
   (a)   Inspect all existing structures to ensure compliance with Municipal
codes and ordinances;
   (b)   Investigate all complaints of violations of the Zoning Code and
housing ordinances, and, more particularly, cases of substandard housing;
   (c)   Inform property owners of violations and endeavor to have such
violations corrected by such property owners;
   (d)   Refer cases of violations, if not timely and reasonably corrected, to
proper authorities for appropriate court action;
   (e)   Make periodic surveys of the community to determine areas of
deterioration or loss of aesthetic values;
   (f)   Maintain accurate and adequate records and reports of all zoning and
housing inspections performed;
   (g)   Enforce all applicable Municipal codes, ordinances and regulations
pertaining to proper and adequate zoning and housing standards;
   (h)   Appear as a witness in all cases involving violations of Municipal
codes and/or ordinances when requested to do so by the Building Commissioner;
and
   (i)   Prepare and perform all related work and enforcement proceedings when
requested to do so by the Building Commissioner.
(Ord. 1973-50. Passed 3-7-73; Ord. 05-180. Passed 12-5-05; Ord. 11-154. Passed
12-20-11.)
1440.05 CLERICAL PERSONNEL.
   There shall be sufficient clerical personnel employed to adequately provide
for the efficient operation of the Division of Buildings. Such personnel shall
be employed and paid in accordance with existing complement and compensation
ordinances. Each individual employed as clerical help shall be qualified in the
areas of typing, data processing and proper procedure in answering complaints
and supplying general information, and shall also be capable of proper methods
of filing and performing related work when directed to do so by the Director of
Community Development.
(Ord. 1973-50. Passed 3-7-73; Ord. 92-27. Passed 1-21-92; Ord. 05-180. Passed
12-5-05; Ord. 11-154. Passed 12-20-11.)
1440.06 RESPONSIBILITY FOR INSPECTIONS.
   Duties and functions relating to inspections shall be performed by the
Backup Inspector in the absence or nonavailability of regular inspectors or if
such positions have not been filled by competent personnel.
(Ord. 1973-50. Passed 3-7-73; Ord. 05-180. Passed 12-5-05; Ord. 11-154. Passed
12-20-11.)
1440.07 DUTIES OF INSPECTORS.
   Any certified individual employed as an inspector in the Division of
Buildings shall perform the duties and functions of such position, whether such
employment is considered full-time or part-time employment.
(Ord. 1973-50. Passed 3-7-73; Ord. 92-27. Passed 1-21-92; Ord. 05-180. Passed
12-5-05; Ord. 11-154. Passed 12-20-11.)
1440.08 EMPLOYMENT AND DISMISSAL OF PERSONNEL.
   The Director of Community Development may, when in his or her judgment
conditions warrant it, dismiss any employee of the Division of Buildings. The
Director of Community Development shall recommend that additional personnel be
employed when conditions warrant it. A final determination of employment of
additional personnel shall be the prerogative of the Mayor, subject to the
existing complement and compensation ordinances.
(Ord. 1973-50. Passed 3-7-73; Ord. 92-27. Passed 1-21-92; Ord. 05-180. Passed
12-5-05; Ord. 11-154. Passed 12-20-11.)

1442.02 TOPOGRAPHIC SURVEY REQUIRED; INSPECTION OF FOOTERS.
   (a)   Each application for a building permit for the erection, construction,
remodeling or alteration of, addition to or moving of any building shall be
accompanied by a topographic survey in a form on file in the Building Division,
which topographic survey shall contain the information shown on such form,
shall be certified by a licensed engineer or surveyor, and shall be examined by
the City Engineer prior to the commencement of any construction.
   (b)   Each applicant shall, upon making application for a building permit in
connection with which a topographic survey is required, pay to the Building
Commissioner, for engineering and inspection services, such fees as are herein
referred to, in addition to all other fees and deposits required. Fees shall be
charged as set forth in
Chapter 214 of the Administration Code for:
      (1)   The inspection of the grade and building setbacks at the footers
when completely formed and before pouring;
      (2)   The inspection when the foundation is topped out and ready for the
plates; and
      (3)   The inspection after final grading.
   (c)   No building permit shall be issued to any applicant unless the
certified topographic survey plan submitted by the applicant has first been
approved by the City Engineer.
   (d)   No construction or erection of, addition to or moving of any building
shall be permitted to proceed after the footers have been formed unless the
City Engineer has approved the grade and setbacks of such footers.
   (e)   In any case wherein an application is made for a building permit to
remodel, make an addition to or alter an existing building, which building was
built in conformity with the grade established by the proper Municipal
authority, the Building Commissioner is hereby authorized to waive the
requirements of a topographic survey with respect to such application if he or
she determines that the remodeling, alteration or addition will be constructed
in conformity with the grade theretofore established.
(Ord. 1970-105. Passed 5-6-70; Ord. 1986-141. Passed 11-19-86.)
1442.03 FEES.
   All building fees and bonds shall be as set forth in Chapter
214 of the Administration Code.
1442.04 NOTIFICATION OF COUNCILPERSONS.
   In the interest of each Councilperson being in a more favorable position to
better serve his or her constituents, the Building Commissioner and the Clerk
of Council are hereby directed to notify, in writing, each Councilperson of
applications for new construction permits, rezoning matters and contemplated
building of any structure which might ultimately result in changing the course
of any drainage ditch or increasing the flow of any drainage ditch. Such
notification shall be given by either the Building Commissioner or the Clerk as
soon as is practicable after such information has been received by his or her
respective office.
(Res. 1972-77. Passed 5-3-72; Ord. 24-141. Passed 9-3-24.)
1442.05 RESPONSIBILITIES OF PERMIT HOLDERS, OWNERS, CONTRACTORS, ETC., RE
MAINTENANCE OF AREAS SURROUNDING CONSTRUCTION SITES.
   (a)   It shall be the responsibility of the permit holder to insure that the
areas surrounding a construction site and the public streets used to access
that site are maintained and properly protected for the health, safety and
welfare of the community.
   (b)   During the time that construction, reconstruction, repair, grading or
landscaping is being done on any premises within the City, the permit holder,
owner, employing contractor and all persons performing work shall be
responsible for the following:
      (1)   The sidewalk, treelawn area, roadway, gutters and storm drains in
front of a construction site shall be kept open and free of building materials,
debris and other nuisances.
      (2)   On new construction a temporary drive capable of supporting
delivery trucks of building material suppliers must be installed.
      (3)   All mud, gravel, sand or other debris tracked onto the roadway must
be removed as soon as possible.
      (4)   All other construction debris accumulated on a particular building
site must be controlled on that site so as not to create a nuisance to
surrounding properties or be distributed throughout the neighborhood.
   (c)   Whoever violates or fails to comply with any of the provisions of this
section, and does not respond to a compliance order of the Building
Commissioner or his or her representative, may be immediately issued a stop-
work order in regard to the offending site or sites and/or be subject to the
penalty provided in Section
1442.99.
(Ord. 93-188. Passed 7-20-93.)
1442.99 PENALTY.
   Whoever violates or fails to comply with any of the provisions of this
chapter is guilty of a minor misdemeanor for a first offense; for a second
offense, such person is guilty of a misdemeanor of the second degree; for a
third or subsequent offense, such person shall be guilty of a misdemeanor of
the first degree. Whoever is convicted of or pleads guilty to a misdemeanor or
minor misdemeanor shall be sentenced in accordance with Section
698.02. A separate offense shall be deemed committed each day during or on
which a violation or noncompliance occurs or continues.
(Ord. 05-13. Passed 3-15-05; Ord. 05-72. Passed 5-17-04.)

1444.01 REGISTRATION REQUIRED.
   (a)   Persons engaged as a contractor in any of the following crafts, trades
and businesses shall be subject to this chapter and may be permitted to engage
in multiple trades providing such trade is similar in nature to such trade:
asphalt/concrete road paving, dry wall/plastering, electrical, excavating and/
or earth moving, general carpentry, H.V.A.C., masonry, painting and/or
decorating, plumbing, sewer, sign, erectors, glazing, landscaping/irrigation,
ornamental iron work, roofing, tile setting, cement, fence, insulation,
demolition, fire suppression, security system, central vac system, pipe fitter,
garage door, utilities, water proofing, fire protection, swimming pool,
clearing, siding contractor, septic tank cleaner, kitchen cabinet, low voltage,
telephone and cable installers, satellite installers, wireless communication/
antenna installers, steel erectors and any specialty contractor not listed,
such as general contractors, street or road builders, etc. Example: A carpenter
may be registered as a carpenter and as such be registered to perform all
carpentry work - build decks, wood fences, framing, cabinetry, drywall, steel
studs, insulation, roofing and window installation upon verification of
experience in such trades.
   (b)   No person shall permit another to contract or engage in any of the
listed trades under his or her registration. Obtaining of permits for an
unregistered contractor shall result in the suspension of the registration of
the contractor responsible for such action.
   (c)   Application for registration shall be obtained from the North Royalton
Building Department and submitted to same for approval by the Building
Commissioner. Such application shall contain the full name of applicant and the
current address of same along with current telephone number. Such application
shall list the names of not more than two employees permitted to obtain permits
for registrant. Each applicant shall submit evidence of three years experience
in said trade by submitting any of the following: federal tax forms, contracts,
licenses of other Municipalities, etc., or in the case of electrical, plumbing,
heating, refrigeration, hydronics, their State Licenses as required by the
State of Ohio to engage in such trades.
(Ord. 1977-56. Passed 5-4-77; Ord. 98-162. Passed 9-1-98; Ord. 99-63. Passed 4-
20-99; Ord. 02-141. Passed 10-1-02; Ord. 05-26. Passed 3-15-05.)
1444.02 APPLICATIONS.
   (a)   Every applicant for registration to engage in the referenced trades
through contracting and/or hire, shall upon the approval of his or her
application furnish and file with the Building Department a performance bond in
the amount as set forth in the fee structure in
Chapter 214 of the Administrative Code for each category of registration. Such
bond shall be in the form of Exhibit A found in Section
1444.09 and shall be approved as to form by the North Royalton Director of Law
and as to sufficiency of surety by the Mayor, guaranteeing full and faithful
compliance by the applicant only to the extent of the bond value with all the
provisions and regulations of applicable building codes of the City, the State
of Ohio or any subdivision thereof now or hereafter having power and authority
to regulate the construction of buildings or other structures within the City.
   (b)   Every applicant for registration shall deposit with the North Royalton
Building Department evidence of a public insurance policy in the amount of one
million dollars ($1,000,000.00) insuring the City or client against any loss or
damage to persons or property from or growing out of work being performed. The
amount of such insurance shall be as set forth in Section
214.08(o) of the Administrative Code (The General Fee Schedule). All policies
shall be subject to the approval of the Director of Law.
(Ord. 1977-56. Passed 5-4-77; Ord. 1989-60. Passed 4-17-89; Ord. 98-163. Passed
9-1-98.; Ord. 02-141. Passed 10-1-02.)
1444.03 FEE; ISSUANCE OF CERTIFICATES OF REGISTRATION.
   Upon approval of an application for registration as a craftsman, contractor
or worker, the applicant shall file with the Building Commissioner the required
bond, properly executed and approved, and shall pay a fee as set forth in
Chapter 214 of the Administration Code for registration as a contractor in each
of the capacities hereinbefore set forth in which he or she desires to operate
within the City, and shall receive from the Building Commissioner a certificate
of registration as a contractor in such capacity as his or her application may
warrant, within the corporate limits of the City, for the current calendar
year.
1444.04 RENEWAL OF CERTIFICATES.
   All certificates of registration shall expire on December 31st of each year.
Certificates may be renewed during the thirty-day period immediately preceding
the expiration date. No certificate shall be issued to any applicant that has
any outstanding violations, pending charges or has been determined to have
failed to comply with any applicable ordinance, statute or directive of the
Building Commissioner and remains in a state of non-compliance. Certificates
may be renewed upon payment of the required fee and presentation of a current
bond and certificate of insurance.
(Ord. 02-141. Passed 10-1-02; Ord. 12-183. Passed 12-18-12.)
1444.05 SUSPENSION OR REVOCATION OF REGISTRATION.
   The Building Commissioner may suspend or revoke any certificate of
registration or renewal thereof issued under this chapter for any of the
following reasons:
   (a)   Misrepresentation of any material fact by the applicant in obtaining
any certificate of registration or the renewal thereof;
   (b)   Use of a certificate of registration to obtain permits for another
person;
   (c)   Faulty or defective workmanship;
   (d)   Departure from or disregard of plans and/or specifications filed with
an application for a building permit;
   (e)   Noncompliance with or violation of any provision of this Building Code
or any other building, plumbing, electrical, sanitary or other code having
application or effect therein; or
   (f)   Construction work of any type done on Sundays, unless written
permission is received from the Building Commissioner.
   No person shall do any work authorized by a certificate of registration when
the same is suspended or revoked.
(Ord. 1977-56. Passed 5-4-77.)
1444.06 NOTICE OF VIOLATIONS; SUSPENSION OR REVOCATION OF CERTIFICATES.
   Notice, in writing, shall be given to a registrant for any noncompliance or
violation by such registrant of any of the provisions of this Building Code or
any other building, plumbing, electrical, sanitary or other code in effect in
the City, discovered by the Building Commissioner or his or her duly authorized
assistants. The registrant shall remedy or cause to be corrected such
noncompliance or violation within five days after the receipt of such notice.
Failure to conform with the orders of the Building Commissioner or his or her
duly authorized assistants shall result in the suspension or revocation of the
registrant's certificate of registration or prosecution as hereinafter
provided, or both.
(Ord. 1977-56. Passed 5-4-77.)
1444.07 APPEALS.
   A registrant whose certificate of registration has been suspended or revoked
may appeal such order of suspension or revocation to the Board of Zoning
Appeals, in writing. The Board shall afford a public hearing upon such appeal,
at which hearing the appellant may be represented by counsel. The appellant and
the Building Commissioner may summon and examine witnesses and introduce
competent testimony pertaining to the reason for suspension or revocation and
to the restoration of a certificate of registration. All such appeals shall be
filed with the Board within five days after receipt of the notice or order from
which an appeal is taken.
(Ord. 1977-56. Passed 5-4-77.)
1444.08 PERFORMANCE OF WORK BY OWNER.
   Nothing in this chapter shall be construed to prevent the owner of any
dwelling, building, structure, premises, lot or parcel of land within the City
from performing any of the work for which registration is hereby required,
without his or her obtaining such registration, on such dwelling, building,
structure, premises, lot or parcel of land so owned, provided such dwelling,
building, structure, premises, lot or parcel of land is for the personal or
private use of said owner and the work performed is not for "speculative" (e.g.
spec. home, model home, etc.) purposes, and further provided that such owner
first obtains a permit to do such work in the manner set forth in this Building
Code, and further provided that the work is done in all respects according to
such Code or any other applicable code and to the plans and specifications
therefor.
(Ord. 91-310. Passed 7-7-92.)
1444.09 PERFORMANCE BOND; ATTACHMENT OF BOND.
   (a)   Every registered contractor shall, as a condition of his or her
registration, file with the Building Commissioner a surety bond in the amount
as set forth in the fee structure in
Chapter 214  of the Administrative Code using the form designated as
Appendix I to Chapter 1444 as follows: the surety bond shall guarantee full and
faithful compliance by the registered contractor with all pertinent laws and
regulations of the State of Ohio and the City, and shall bind the surety
thereon to correct or abate any violation of said laws or regulations whenever
the registered contractor named as the principal on such bond refuses,
neglects, or fails to correct or abate such violation within a reasonable time
limit set by the Building Commissioner. The bond shall be required for all work
to be performed by the registered contractor involving residential or non-
residential structures.
   (b)   Whenever a registered contractor has been cited by the Building
Commissioner or his or her agent for a violation of the laws and regulations of
the State of Ohio or the City, the Building Commissioner shall notify the
registered contractor that the violation requires immediate correction and that
the surety bond will be in jeopardy absent such correction. Notice of violation
shall be in writing and delivered in person or by registered mail to the
address shown in the contractor's registration.
   (c)   If the Building Commissioner determines that, after delivering a
notice under subsection (b) hereof, a registered contractor has failed to take
action to correct the violation in accordance with the time limits established
by the Building Commissioner, the Building Commissioner may notify the
registered contractor that he or she intends to pursue attachment of the
contractor’s surety bond. Notice of attachment shall be in writing and
delivered in person or by mail to the address shown in the contractor's
registration.
   (d)   Within three business days of delivery of the notice of attachment,
the registered contractor may request a hearing before the Building
Commissioner for the purpose of disputing either that a violation exists or
that proper action has not been taken to correct the violation. If a request
for a hearing is made in writing, the Building Commissioner shall hold a
hearing within five business days of receiving such request.
   (e)   If no request has been timely received for a hearing under subsection
(d) hereof, or if, following such a hearing, the Building Commissioner finds
that a violation does exist and that the registered contractor has not taken
action to correct it, the City may then proceed to make the corrections itself
by its own labor or by contracting out for such corrections. All costs incurred
by the City in making such corrections may be paid from the bond in the name of
the registered contractor. If, after making such deductions, there remains a
balance due to the City, the City shall be free to pursue other legal recourse
available to obtain full reimbursement.
   (f)   The Building Commissioner may relinquish the City's rights under the
performance bond and assign those rights to any person, firm, or corporations
with whom the contractor has contracted, provided that the Building
Commissioner determines that no municipal action or expenditure is required to
correct the violation.
   (g)   Any property owner holding an open permit with the contractor shall be
notified of the City's relinquishment of its right to claim under the bond. Any
such person, firm, or corporation may proceed to seek their proportional
damages under the performance bond.
(Ord. 05-26. Passed 3-15-05; Ord. 14-126. Passed 11-5-14.)
1444.99 PENALTY.
   Whoever violates or fails to comply with any of the provisions of this
chapter is guilty of a minor misdemeanor. Whoever is convicted of or pleads
guilty to a misdemeanor, or minor misdemeanor shall be sentenced in accordance
with Section
698.02. A separate offense shall be deemed committed each day during or on
which a violation or noncompliance occurs or continues.
(Ord. 05-13. Passed 3-15-05.)

CHAPTER 1446
Certificates of Occupancy
1446.01   Action of Building Commissioner.

1446.03   Short form lease agreement.

   Building and Housing Code fees - see ADM.
214.08
   Division of Buildings - see B. & H. Ch.
1440
   Building permits - see B. & H. Ch.
1442
1446.01 ACTION OF BUILDING COMMISSIONER.
   (a)   All applications for certificates of occupancy must be presented to
the Building Commissioner or his or her authorized representative by the owner
of the building or premises or his or her agent. Such applications shall
contain all the data deemed necessary by the Building Commissioner to indicate
that the construction of the Building and the occupancy of the premises conform
to all applicable laws, ordinances, rules and regulations of the Municipality.
   (b)   The Building Commissioner or his or her authorized representative
shall issue a certificate of occupancy within five days after all requirements
have been satisfied.
(Ord. 1978-110. Passed 4-19-78.)
1446.02 WHEN REQUIRED.
   A certificate of occupancy must be obtained as a condition precedent to the
occupancy and/or use of a building, structure and land under the following
circumstances:
   (a)   Occupancy of a Building Erected or Altered. A certificate of occupancy
shall be required before occupancy of a new building or before occupancy of an
existing building which has been altered, moved, changed in use or increased in
off-street parking requirements. Such certificate shall only be issued after
the erection or alteration of the building, or a component thereof, or after a
required accessory use has been provided and found upon inspection to be in
conformity with this chapter and this Building Code.
   (b)   Change in Use of Conforming Building or Land. A certificate of
occupancy shall be required before occupancy of a conforming building or land
where the use has been changed, provided the use is different than the prior
use, and shall be issued when found upon inspection that such building or land
is in conformity with the Zoning Code and this Building Code.
   (c)   Change in Use of Nonconforming Building or Land. A certificate of
occupancy shall be required whenever a nonconforming building or land is
changed, and shall not be issued until such building or land is found to be in
conformity with the requirements of the Zoning Code dealing with nonconforming
uses.
(Ord. 1972-189. Passed 4-4-73.)
1446.03 SHORT FORM LEASE AGREEMENT.
   All applications for a certificate of occupancy shall have attached to them
a copy of a short form lease agreement which has been entered into by the owner
and the prospective tenant.
(Ord. 1972-189. Passed 4-4-73.)
1446.04 POSTING.
   Upon receipt of a certificate of occupancy, an owner or his or her agent
shall immediately thereafter cause such certificate to be posted in a
conspicuous place on the subject premises.
(Ord. 1972-189. Passed 4-4-73.)
1446.05 CONTENTS.
   A certificate of occupancy shall contain the following information:
   (a)   The type of occupancy permitted for the premises, or types of
occupancy permitted if there is more than one tenant occupying the premises;
   (b)   The maximum permissible live loads permitted for each floor of the
premises;
   (c)   The maximum number of occupants that can be accommodated in the
premises by virtue of limitations designated on the occupancy permit; and
   (d)   Any other information deemed necessary and pertinent by the Building
Commissioner.
(Ord. 1972-189. Passed 4-4-73.)
1446.06 RECORDS.
   A record of all applications and certificates of occupancy issued shall be
kept on file in the office of the Building Commissioner, and copies thereof
shall be furnished, upon request, to any person having a proprietary or tenancy
interest in the building or land affected.
(Ord. 1972-189. Passed 4-4-73.)
1446.07 CONFLICT OF LAWS.
   In all cases wherein any of the provisions of this chapter conflict with any
of the provisions of a technical code adopted by the City, the more restrictive
provision shall control, except for provisions of the Ohio Building Code, which
shall control in all events.
(Ord. 06-32. Passed 2-21-06.)
1446.99 PENALTY.
   Whoever violates or fails to comply with any of the provisions of this
chapter is guilty of a minor misdemeanor. Whoever is convicted of or pleads
guilty to a misdemeanor, or minor misdemeanor shall be sentenced in accordance
with Section
698.02. A separate offense shall be deemed committed each day during or on
which a violation or noncompliance occurs or continues.
(Ord. 05-13. Passed 3-15-05.)

1448.01 POSTING REQUIRED IN SUBDIVISIONS.
   (a)   No developer of a subdivision, builder constructing buildings within a
subdivision, or person, firm or corporation being the agent of a developer or
builder in the sale of lots within a subdivision, shall sell a lot or construct
a building without first having posted within a designated sales office or
within a temporary construction office of such builder or developer the
following:
      (1)   A copy of the final plat of the subdivision which has been approved
for recording purposes only by the Planning Commission, Council and other
required administrative officials of the City;
      (2)   A topographical map clearly showing thereon grades, elevations,
easements, open ditches, swales, creeks, walkways and any other land
characteristics of the subdivision that may be of concern to a prospective
purchaser;
      (3)   A copy of all declarations of covenants and deed restrictions which
have been recorded with the Cuyahoga County Recorder and which run with the
land;
      (4)   A copy of any nonprofit homeowners' association charter and rules
and regulations, if any, which may be applicable to the homeowners within the
subdivision;
(Ord. 91-269. Passed 11-19-91.)
      (5)   Maps, plats or plans designating all boundaries, structures, uses
and zoning classifications related to property contiguous to the subdivision
and the sublot being considered for purchase; and
      (6)   Written information identifying the public school district serving
the subdivision and sublot.
   (b)   Every developer of a subdivision, builder constructing buildings
within a subdivision, or person, firm or corporation being the agent of a
developer or builder in the sale of lots within a subdivision, shall require
that all prospective purchasers of lots and/or buildings within the subdivision
execute and sign a certificate approved for use by the City stating therein
that such prospective purchaser has been shown, has reviewed and has been
informed of or has otherwise received, all of the plats, plans, documents, maps
and documents specified in subsection (a) hereof, before the sale of a lot or
building in the subdivision has been made. The signed certificate shall be
attached to any application for a building permit submitted to the Building
Department.
(Ord. 91-269. Passed 11-19-91; Ord. 02-172. Passed 12-3-02.)

1448.99 PENALTY.
   Whoever violates or fails to comply with any of the provisions of this
chapter is guilty of a minor misdemeanor for a first offense; for a second

CHAPTER 1458
Carbon Monoxide Detectors
1458.01   Installation required.
1458.02   Installation specifications.
1458.03   Inspections.
1458.04   Rules and regulations.
1458.05   Connections to electrical system.
1458.99   Penalty.
   CROSS REFERENCES
   Smoke detection system for apartments and condominiums - see Ohio R.C.
3781.104
   Clean indoor air - see GEN. OFF. Ch.
620
   Campfires - see GEN. OFF.
660.21
   Setting fires; grills and barbecues - see F.P.
1610.09
   Open burning - see F.P. Ch.
1620
1458.01 INSTALLATION REQUIRED.
   (a)   Carbon monoxide detectors shall be installed in all new residential
dwelling units and other locations provided herein:
      (1)   All single-family homes.
      (2)   All Multifamily housing units.
      (3)   All apartment units that are served by a self-contained heating
plant or furnace that is installed within the individual apartment unit.
   (b)   A carbon monoxide detector shall be installed in or adjacent to all
common laundry areas and/or boiler/heating areas where fossil fuel appliances
are installed in all apartment buildings and all multifamily dwelling
structures. Compliance with this subsection shall be made by September 1, 1996.
The Bureau of Fire Prevention shall inspect and approve the location and
installation of these required carbon monoxide detectors.
(Ord. 96-99. Passed 4-16-96.)
1458.02 INSTALLATION SPECIFICATIONS.
   (a)   At least one carbon monoxide detector shall be installed in each
dwelling unit as listed in Section
1458.01.
   (b)   Carbon monoxide detectors shall be installed in the manner and in the
recommended locations specified by the manufacturer. Every carbon monoxide
detector shall comply with all applicable Federal and State regulations and
bear the label of a nationally recognized testing laboratory, and shall meet
the standards of UL-2034 or its equivalent.
    (c)   Additional carbon monoxide detection units may be necessary to insure
maximum protection in large homes or homes with multiple levels of living
space.
(Ord. 96-99. Passed 4-16-96.)
1458.03 INSPECTIONS.
   The Bureau of Fire Prevention shall inspect and approve the installation of
carbon monoxide detectors as specified in this chapter for all new single and
multifamily dwelling units and shall issue a report to the Building
Commissioner acknowledging compliance with this chapter prior to the issuance
of an occupancy permit by the Building Department. The Building Commissioner
shall have concurrent jurisdiction with the Chief of the Fire Department to
inspect the installation of any carbon monoxide detector required to be
installed by this chapter.
(Ord. 96-99. Passed 4-16-96.)
1458.04 RULES AND REGULATIONS.
   The Building Commissioner shall issue rules and regulations consistent with
the provisions of this chapter for the implementation and administration of the
provisions of this chapter.
(Ord. 96-99. Passed 4-16-96.)
1458.05 CONNECTIONS TO ELECTRICAL SYSTEM.
   No carbon monoxide detector or an alternative system shall be directly
connected (permanently wired) to the electrical system of a structure, unless
an electrical permit has first been obtained from the Building Department.
(Ord. 96-99. Passed 4-16-96.)
1458.99 PENALTY.
   Whoever violates or fails to comply with any of the provisions of this
chapter is guilty of a misdemeanor of the first degree and shall be fined not
more than one thousand dollars ($1,000) or imprisoned not more than six months,
or both, for each offense. A separate offense shall be deemed committed each
day during or on which a violation occurs or continues.

1460.01 GARBAGE DISPOSAL SYSTEMS.
   (a)   No single residence or home shall be constructed unless the structure
is equipped with an appropriate digester-type garbage disposal unit.
   (b)   No multifamily dwelling, rental unit or apartment house shall be
constructed unless the structure is equipped with a digester-type garbage
disposal unit for each family unit or rental unit.
   (c)   No commercial building shall be constructed unless the structure
contains a digester-type garbage disposal unit, except that such digester need
be installed only in that type of commercial building designed or equipped for,
or whose intended use includes, the storing, sheltering, preparation,
consumption or sale of food or foodstuffs.
   (d)   No commercial building or multifamily dwelling building shall be
constructed unless such building has a sufficient storage area for refuse or
garbage. If such storage area is outside of the building, such area shall be
enclosed by masonry walls, redwood fencing or other suitable materials to
completely conceal and contain the articles and containers placed therein.
(Ord. 1978-332. Passed 12-6-78.)
1460.02 AUTHORITY OF BUILDING COMMISSIONER.
   The Building Commissioner shall determine the following:
   (a)   Whether a digester-type garbage disposal unit shall be required in the
proposed structure for which an application for a building permit is pending;
   (b)   The system or type of equipment and apparatus that can be used by an
applicant for a building permit for the disposal of garbage in his or her
proposed structure;
   (c)   The manner of installation of the equipment; and
   (d)   The standards of operating efficiency, the specifications as to size
and other similar standards and specifications which relate to the safe and
sanitary installation and operation of the equipment.
(Ord. 1978-332. Passed 12-6-78.)
1460.03 COMPACTORS.
   (a)   Required. All commercial and industrial establishments which, by the
nature of their business, generate volumes of trash which preclude the use of
the usual disposal methods (dumpsters, etc.), shall have installed a compactor
system for this use. Bundled trash shall not be stored for longer than seven
consecutive days.
   (b)   Specifications. For purposes of this chapter, the following
specifications are prescribed for garbage and trash compactors:
      (1)   They must be of a type that has been tested and approved by
Underwriters Laboratories, Inc.
      (2)   They must be installed in accordance with the National Electrical
Code, as adopted in Section
1424.01.
      (3)   They must bear the seal of Underwriters Laboratories, Inc., or
another certifying body.
(Ord. 93-134. Passed 5-18-93.)
1460.04 INCINERATORS.
   All incinerators presently being utilized for garbage or trash disposal
purposes shall be kept and maintained in good repair as otherwise set forth in
these Codified Ordinances. Effective September 30, 1994, the use of
incinerators for such purposes shall be prohibited.
(Ord. 94-143. Passed 7-5-94.)
1460.05 RIGHT OF ENTRY FOR INSPECTION.
   The Building Commissioner or his or her duly authorized representative may
enter and inspect any premises for the purpose of investigating the
installation of garbage and trash compactors.
(Ord. 94-143. Passed 7-5-94.)
1460.06 WATER PRESSURE REDUCING VALVES
   No residential building shall be constructed unless the structure is
equipped with an approved water pressure reducing valve that can maintain
pressure at 80 pounds or less.
(Ord 99-129. Passed 9-7-99)
1460.99 PENALTY.
   Whoever violates or fails to comply with any of the provisions of this
chapter is guilty of a minor misdemeanor. Whoever is convicted of or pleads
guilty to a misdemeanor, or minor misdemeanor shall be sentenced in accordance
with Section
698.02. A separate offense shall be deemed committed each day during or on
which a violation or noncompliance occurs or continues.
(Ord. 05-13. Passed 3-15-05.)
CHAPTER 1462

   CROSS REFERENCES
   Determination of grade levels - see ADM.
204.01
   Building and Housing Code fees - see ADM.

   Return of notices to Mayor for construction of sidewalks, curbs or gutters -
see ADM.
230.03

   Grading - see B. & H. Ch.
1468

1480
1462.01 APPLICATION OF CHAPTER.
   This chapter shall be applicable to the construction of any City sidewalk,
residential driveway, driveway apron, parking area and residential sidewalk
which connects with any of the other types of structures set forth in this
section.
(Ord. 1984-112. Passed 7-5-84.)
1462.02 CONCRETE USAGE; QUALITY.
   All concrete used for any of the purposes set forth in this chapter shall:
   (a)   Contain a cement content of six and one-half bag mix at ninety-four
pounds per bag of Portland cement;
   (b)   Have an air entrainment of six percent to eight percent at the time of
pour;
   (c)   Consist of sound coarse aggregate one inch or smaller;
   (d)   Contain no more water than will permit a slump between a minimum of
four inches and a maximum of six inches;
   (e)   Have a minimum thickness of four inches in the driveway and six inches
in the apron from the property line to the curb or street line; and
   (f)   Be reinforced with wire reinforcing mesh having a maximum spacing of
six inches in either parallel direction between the wires and a minimum wire
size of number 10 U.S. gauge.
(Ord. 1984-112. Passed 7-5-84.)
1462.03 CURING; FINISHING; MIXING.
   (a)   A curing compound must be applied immediately after broom finishing,
without damaging the surface, according to manufacturer's recommendations.
   (b)   Calcium or other admixtures shall not be added at the job site.
   (c)   A broom finish shall be required. Finishing must be delayed until
water sheen (bleed water) has disappeared from the surface.
   (d)   Cement shall not be dusted upon a plastic-like surface.
   (e)   Water shall not be sprinkled upon a surface as a finishing aid.
(Ord. 1984-112. Passed 7-5-84.)
1462.04 BASE.
   (a)   The base shall be smooth and shall consist of undisturbed or compacted
earth. A stone, gravel, limestone screening or nonsettling material approved by
the Building Commissioner may be used as a leveling course. Excavations or
trenches under a drive must be compacted and filled with a nonsettling
material. Fills shall be placed in four-inch lifts and each lift shall be
compacted. Use of foundry byproducts will not be permitted.
   (b)   The subgrade or base shall be dampened if dry before pouring.
(Ord. 1984-112. Passed 7-5-84.)
1462.05 JOINTS.
   (a)   Control joints, whether hand tooled or sawn, shall be to a depth of
one-fourth the thickness of the slab. The dimensions of any control panel shall
not exceed ten feet.
(Ord. 1984-112. Passed 7-5-84.)
   (b)   Isolation joints shall be required where concrete abuts any structure,
including, but not limited to, foundations, garage floors, stoops, paved
streets and City sidewalks. A superior method of construction, particularly
where concrete work abuts a stoop, may be approved by the Building
Commissioner.
(Ord. 93-135. Passed 5-18-93.)
1462.06 TIME OF POUR.
   (a)   Where the temperature in the surrounding area is below seventy degrees
Fahrenheit, the maximum allowable time from load to pour shall be one and one-
half hours.
   (b)   Where the temperature in the surrounding area is above seventy degrees
Fahrenheit, the maximum allowable time from loading to pour shall be one hour.
   (c)   When concrete is placed at or below an atmospheric temperature of
forty degrees Fahrenheit, or whenever the predicted temperature will fall below
forty degrees Fahrenheit within the curing period, the water or aggregate, or
both, shall be heated and suitable enclosures and heating devices shall be
provided. The concrete shall be placed at a temperature of not less than fifty
degrees Fahrenheit and not more than seventy degrees Fahrenheit, and the air
surrounding the forms and deposited concrete shall be maintained within this
temperature range for not less than five days.
   (d)   When the atmospheric temperature is forecast for fifty degrees
Fahrenheit or less, curing compounds shall not be used, but a sealer in a
mixture of fifty percent boiled linseed oil and fifty percent turpentine or
mineral spirits shall be used.
(Ord. 1984-112. Passed 7-5-84.)
1462.07 RESIDENTIAL CONCRETE DRIVE: PLANT AND CONTRACTOR'S REPORT.
   (a)   In any construction within the application of this chapter, all
supplies shall, at the time of loading for delivery to a user, complete a form
entitled the Residential Concrete Drive: Plant and Contractor's Report. Part I
shall state:
      (1)   Delivery destination;
      (2)   Size of load;
      (3)   Concrete mix;
      (4)   Air entrainment;
      (5)   Amount of water added at plant;
      (6)   Admixture added;
      (7)   Amount of calcium chloride added; and
      (8)   Time of truck loading.
   (b)   In any construction within the application of this chapter, the
contractor or his or her agent shall complete a form entitled the Residential
Concrete Drive: Plant and Contractor's Report. Part II shall state:
      (1)   The address or sublot number of the pour location;
      (2)   The time of arrival;
      (3)   The time of pour;
      (4)   The name of the builder or user;
      (5)   The name of the cement contractor or user;
      (6)   The amount of water at the time of pour;
      (7)   The area temperature at the time of pour; and
      (8)   The curing compound used and the type of sealer used.
   (c)   An original and two copies of the Report shall be signed by the
individuals completing the report. Such persons do, by affixing their
signatures to this Report, warrant that the statements contained therein are
true under penalty of law. The original shall be sent to the Building
Commissioner, a copy shall be sent to the builder and a copy shall be retained
by the supplier.
(Ord. 1984-112. Passed 7-5-84.)
1462.08 INSPECTIONS; FEES.
   (a)   The City Engineer or his or her representative shall inspect the site
of proposed construction under this chapter prior to commencement thereof,
including, but not limited to, removal of an existing structure. The issuance
of a building permit shall be contingent on such inspection. The City Engineer
shall also inspect all forms prior to the pouring of any concrete structure.
   (b)   The Building Commissioner or his or her representative shall inspect
and supervise the actual pouring of any structure regulated in this chapter.
   (c)   Each inspection required herein shall require a minimum of twenty-four
hours notice to the appropriate City department.
   (d)   Fees shall be as set forth in
Chapter 214 of the Administration Code.
(Ord. 1984-112. Passed 7-5-84.)
1462.99 PENALTY.
   Whoever violates or fails to comply with any of the provisions of this
chapter is guilty of a misdemeanor of the fourth degree and shall be fined not
more than two hundred fifty dollars ($250.00) or imprisoned not more than
thirty days, or both, for each offense. A separate offense shall be deemed
committed each day during or on which a violation or noncompliance occurs or
continues.
CHAPTER 1464
Exterior Property Maintenance
1464.01   Title.

   Power to regulate building sanitation - see Ohio R.C. 715.29
   Nuisances - see Ohio R.C. Ch. 3767
   Noxious odors; filthy accumulations - see GEN. OFF.
